commitResults.messageTitle: Improve DELETE validation and user guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
The DELETE command reports generic errors for malformed and invalid
index inputs.

Users need specific feedback to understand whether the index is missing,
malformed, duplicated, or out of range.

Handle DELETE argument validation for missing, extra, non-integer,
non-positive, and out of range indexes. Add tests for the new behaviour
and update the User Guide to document common errors.

commitResults.messageBody:
The DELETE command documentation and tests do not fully reflect its
current parsing behaviour and displayed-list semantics.

Improve test coverage and documentation so users and developers receive
clear, consistent guidance when deleting contacts.

Update DELETE parser tests for whitespace-only arguments and single-token
invalid input, remove the stale parser-test comment, and standardise
DELETE messages and documentation to use “contact”.

Update the DELETE use case in the Developer Guide to document its
preconditions, successful flow, empty-list handling, and invalid-index
errors.

implementation, where indexes refer to the currently displayed contact
list.

DELETE currently describes a single displayed contact using the range
`1-1`, which is awkward for users.

Display `valid index: 1` when only one contact is displayed, while
retaining the range format for lists with multiple contacts.

Add tests covering both single-contat and multiple-contact out-of-range
errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle ignored arguments in LIST command
commitResults.messageBody:
The LIST command accepts additional arguments without informing users.
This may cause users to assume that arguments such as `list 3` have a
purpose, such as displaying only the first three contacts. The behaviour
for empty address books and search filters is also not clearly
communicated.

Add a dedicated `ListCommandParser` to detect meaningful additional
arguments, display a warning that they are ignored, reset active search
filters, and report when no contacts are available.

Treat whitespace-only arguments as empty input so trailing whitespace
does not trigger a warning. Add command, parser, and end-to-end tests,
and update the User Guide and Developer Guide to document the behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for prefixed name searches in FindCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command accepts only unprefixed, space-separated name keywords.

This prevents users from searching for multi-word name phrases and does
not provide a consistent syntax for adding future role and tag filters.

Support n/ prefixed name searches while preserving legacy
space-separated searches. Reject missing criteria, blank n/ values,
mixed search modes, and unrecognised prefixes.

Use ArgumentTokenizer to extract repeated n/ values and retain each
prefixed value as one phrase. Establish the prefix-based syntax for
future r/ and t/ search filters.

Add parser tests covering legacy searches, prefixed phrases, repeated
prefixes, whitespace handling, and invalid input cases.

Add RoleContainsKeywordsPredicate for role-based contact filtering
commitResults.messageBody:
The model layer only provides NameContainsKeywordsPredicate to filter
contacts by name. There is no predicate available to filter contacts
based on assigned role.

The upcoming role-based search feature requires a dedicated predicate
that evaluates whether a contact's role matches user-supplied keywords.

Create RoleContainsKeywordsPredicate, similar to
NameContainsKeywordsPredicate, to test if a contact's role contains
search keywords as case-insensitive substrings.

Add comprehensive unit tests in RoleContainsKeywordsPredicateTest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update FindCommand to support multiple search predicates
commitResults.messageBody:
FindCommand only accepts a single NameContainsKeywordPRedicate and
filters the person list based on that single condition.

Supporting multi-criteria searches (such as finding contacts who match
both a specific name and a specific role) requires FindCommand to
evaluate multiple predicates concurrently.

Modify FindCommand's constructor to accept a varargs parameter of
Predicate<Person>. Stores the predicates in a list and validate that at
least one non-null predicate is provided.
Update execute to filter the person list to match all predicates.

Add tests in FindCommandTest.

commitResults.messageBody:
FindCommandParser only recognises the n/ prefix for names and unprefixed
legacy keywords. Any input containing the r/ prefix is treated as an
unrecognised prefix or invalid argument.

Users need the CLI syntax to perform role-based searches as well well as
combined name and role searches using the r/ prefix.

Update FindCommandParser to recognise PREFIX_ROLE alongside existing
PREFIX_NAME.

Add comprehensive tests in FindCommandParserTest covering single r/,
multiple r/, combined n/ and r/, and invalid syntax.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TagContainsKeywordsPredicate for tag-based contact filtering
commitResults.messageBody:
The model layer only provides predicates to filter contacts by name and
role. There is no predicate available to filter contacts based on their
assigned tags.

The upcoming tag-based search features requires an isolated predicate
that evaluates whether any of a contact's tags match user-supplied
search keywords. Without this predicate, the model cannot search by tag.

Create TagContainsKeywordsPredicate implementing Predicate<Person> to
test if any of a contact's tags contain search keywords as
case-insensitive substrings.

Add comprehensive unit tests in TagContainsKeywordsPredicateTest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update Model to support sorting the displayed contact list
commitResults.messageBody:
The model exposes a filtered contact list.

Sorting needs to change the displayed order so contact indices match
what users see, while preserving the saved order of contacts.

Support sorting in Model and ModelManager, cover ordering and contact
updates with tests.

The model supports sorting the displayed contact list, but no command
defines how users' chosen fields affect the displayed order.

Users need to view all contacts sorted by name, role, or both, with the
first specified field taking priority.

Let's:
* add SortCommand with case-insensitive name and role sorting
* use subsequent fields to break ties in earlier fields
* show all contacts when sorting, regardless of the active filter
* provide feedback when the address book is empty
* test constructor validation, field priority, case handling, filter
  clearing, and replacement of an existing sort order

Keep sort criteria in priority order so users can choose which field
takes precendence. Apply sorting through the model's displayed view so
contact indices follow the order shown without changing saved data.

Use unit tests for command construction and equality, and integration
tests with ModelManager to verify execution behaviour.

Command parsing and registration follow in a separate commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add argument parsing and command registration
commitResults.messageBody:
SortCommand supports ordered sorting criteria, but users cannot invoke
it through the application's command parser.

Users need to select name or role sorting, specifying their priority,
and receive clear feedback for invalid syntax.

Let's:
* register sort with the main command parser
* parser n/ and r/ in the order supplied
* default to name sorting when no arguments are supplied
* reject duplicate fields, attached values, and unexpected arguments
* document the default and case-insensitive behaviour in command usage
* add parser and command-dispatch tests

Treat each field as a standalone token so its position determines
sorting priority and unexpected arguments cannot be silently ignored.

commitResults.messageBody:
Sorting changes displayed contact indices and remains active during
subsequent commands.

These interactions need regression coverage to ensure commands target
the intended contacts and preserve address-book data and history.

Let's,
* test editing and deleting contacts using sorted indices
* verify name and role edits reposition contacts correctly
* test sorting alongside filtering, listing, undo, and redo
* verify sorting preserves redo history and saved contact order
* check that equal sort keys preserve distinct contact identities
* strengthen filtering and empty-argument coverage

Use complete command sequences through LogicManager to verify that
parsing, execution, model updates, and storage work together.

Both checkstyle tasks pass, and the suite reports 619 passing tests.

Currently, NameContainsKeywordsPredicate only matches whole words

Currently, VersionedAddressBook exists in isolation from Model
and ModelManager. Given that a future undo/redo command must
be provided the model as a parameter, we need to integrate our
VersionedAddressBook into Model and ModelManager.

Let's first start small and specify the updated contract in
Model.java.

Currently, the Model's interface has been updated, but the new
methods have not been implemented in ModelManager. This currently
raises a compilation error since ModelManager has not implemented
the new methods.

Let's implement the new methods in ModelManager.

Currently, ModelManagerTest does not include tests for the 5 new
methods implemented in ModelManager. Let's change that so that
the new methods are covered by tests.

Also, the ModelStub inner class of AddCommandTest that implements
Model currently cannot be compiled because the 5 methods are not
implemented. Let's provide the implementations for this stub in
the same format as the other abstract methods in Model.

With ModelManager having a VersionedAddressBook, the overriden
equals method for ModelManager will also check if their
VersionedAddressBook are equal, which requires addressBookStateList
to be equal, on top of two AddressBooks having the same current state.

This new requirement raises regressions in LogicManagerTest, where
expectedModel does not share the same history as the current Model
it is compared to.

Let's change the usage of expectedModel in these tests, making sure
that the test purposes remain unchanged.

Currently, the overridden equals method in VersionedAddressBook
does not have 100% test coverage because the currentStatePointer
equality condition isn't isolated and tested.

Let's add a test case that checks between two VersionedAddressBook
with the same current state, same history and different state pointers,
and confirm that VersionedAddressBook is fully covered.

Add commitAddressBook() calls after successful add, delete, edit and
clear operations to record undo/redo history. Validation failures
leave history unchanged.

The addition of state saving in the mutating commands (add, edit,
delete, clear) caused unit tests in LogicManagerTest,

DeleteCommandTest and EditCommandTest to fail. These failures arise
often due to the expectedModel not having its new state committed.

Let's make changes to ensure the tests pass and that these tests
still uphold their original purpose.
